content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | DevOps & Platform Engineering
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Owns CI pipelines and ephemeral test environments used by three product teams. Hands-on experience with Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, alongside personal projects using Terraform and GitOps. Moving toward a full-time DevOps or platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access; basic)
Infrastructure as Code & Platforms: Terraform (personal projects), k3s, Argo CD, Ansible (basic)
Monitoring & Security: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, cert-manager, TLS certificates
Programming & Data: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, PostgreSQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems & Tools: Linux, Git, AWS (learning: EC2 and S3 basics)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, as well as artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request environments for applications, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster; environments are removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Enable QA and product teams to review changes before merge, with end-to-end tests running against the ephemeral environments.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and collected CI test results into PostgreSQL for Grafana flaky-test dashboards.
- Wrote an internal guide to CI pipelines used in onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Performed manual and automated testing of web and mobile applications for client projects.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues in logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Delivered short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments with seeded data, deployed through Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
- Automated environment cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity, enabling feature reviews and end-to-end testing before merge.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and split end-to-end tests into a separate stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATIONS
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible and well-structured CV. It presents a clear transition from QA automation into DevOps/platform engineering, uses quantified outcomes, and distinguishes professional infrastructure work from personal projects. The strongest evidence is the ownership of GitLab CI pipelines, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, measurable pipeline improvements, and test reliability improvements. The document is also appropriately transparent about limitations such as namespace-level Kubernetes access, basic Terraform/Ansible experience, AWS learning, and the scheduled rather than completed CKA exam. Minor weaknesses are that the summary could foreground stakeholder leadership and technical documentation more directly, and some bullets could use slightly more consistent action-oriented grammar.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, readable text formatting, standard technology names, clear chronology, and relevant keywords such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, AWS, Linux, TLS, PostgreSQL, Python and Bash. The separate Selected Infrastructure Projects section is particularly useful for surfacing DevOps evidence. AI/ATS screening probability is moderate-to-good for general junior or mid-level DevOps/platform roles, but lower for this specific vacancy because strict screening may look for strong Terraform, Terragrunt, system design, networking, mTLS and cloud operations. The CV correctly does not claim Terragrunt, mTLS, production cluster administration or passed Kubernetes certification. No parsing or formatting defect is apparent.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with hands-on infrastructure engineering, CI/CD ownership, Kubernetes-based environment delivery, Linux, TLS certificate tooling, analytical improvement work, technical documentation and collaboration with QA/product teams. It also shows AWS exposure at a learning level and a JVM-adjacent background through Java test automation. The main candidate-level gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt experience, explicit systems architecture/system design experience, networking and mTLS, production cloud operation, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack engineering. These are gaps in the candidate's documented background rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. The role also appears to expect a more experienced cloud infrastructure profile than the candidate's stated target of junior/mid-level DevOps or platform engineering.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR — In the Professional Summary, revise the final two sentences to make the strongest role-relevant evidence more prominent without overstating seniority. For example: "Owns CI/CD pipelines and ephemeral Kubernetes test environments used by three product teams, with hands-on experience in Docker, Helm, Terraform personal projects, GitOps, monitoring and TLS certificate management. Transitioning from QA automation into a junior-to-mid-level DevOps or platform engineering role." 

MINOR — In the Odrava Health experience section, change "Enable QA and product teams to review changes before merge" to the grammatically complete, more outcome-focused wording: "Enabled QA and product teams to review changes before merge and run end-to-end tests against ephemeral environments." This more clearly supports the requirement for bringing stakeholders along.

MINOR — In the Odrava Health experience section, revise the internal documentation bullet to make technical communication and knowledge sharing more searchable: "Authored and maintained an internal CI/CD guide used in onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023." 

MINOR — In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, keep the explicit scope limitation in the Kubernetes evidence, because it is truthful and valuable: retain wording such as "deployed through Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster" rather than implying cluster administration. Also ensure the Terraform bullet continues to identify the Hetzner VPS as a personal project, since the original information does not support professional cloud Terraform experience.

MINOR — In the Technical Skills section, consider changing "AWS (learning: EC2 and S3 basics)" to "AWS — learning projects: EC2 and S3 basics" so the learning-only status is immediately clear while retaining the ATS keywords. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, VPC/network design, or production AWS operations because they are not supported by the candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, professional, and strongly quantified. The strongest evidence is the ownership of GitLab CI for three teams, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, the 30% runner-cost reduction, and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The selected infrastructure projects effectively support the transition from QA automation toward DevOps/platform engineering. The main content weakness is that the document presents several relevant behaviours—technical ownership, analytical investigation, documentation, and mentoring—but does not consistently connect them to the job's language of leading technical topics, stakeholder alignment, system design, and reliable/secure platform operation. The career-transition wording is honest, but it also makes the candidate appear more junior than the evidence in the experience section suggests.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly section headings, standard reverse-chronological structure, plain text bullets, and searchable technology names. It should parse reliably. Keyword coverage is good for GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Linux, TLS, PostgreSQL, Python, and Java. AI screening probability is moderate to good for a junior/mid-level DevOps or platform role, but lower for this particular contractor role because the CV does not show Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, cloud production operation, or explicit networking/security terminology. The wording “Terraform (personal projects)” and “AWS (learning...)” is appropriately transparent and should be retained. There is no evidence of hallucinated skills or experience when compared with the original candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a credible adjacent match rather than a strong direct match for the advertised cloud infrastructure contractor role. It shows hands-on infrastructure-related work through GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, ephemeral environments, monitoring, TLS certificate management, and personal Terraform/GitOps work. It also shows ownership, analytical improvement, documentation, mentoring, and communication through the internal CI guide and onboarding use. AWS is shown at a learning/basic level. The candidate's material indicates gaps in strong Terraform/Terragrunt experience, mTLS, broader system architecture/design, production cloud operation, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack development. These are candidate-experience gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting the CV. The CV should nevertheless make the supported evidence more explicit and use the job's terminology where truthful.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified; the CV is consistent with the Original Candidate Information and does not appear to invent skills, certifications, or experience.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence, “Moving toward a full-time DevOps or platform engineering role,” with wording that foregrounds the evidence already documented, for example: “Owns CI/CD pipelines and ephemeral Kubernetes test environments for three product teams, with hands-on experience in Docker, Helm, GitLab CI, monitoring, and personal Terraform/GitOps projects; targeting a junior-to-mid-level DevOps or platform engineering role.” This is more aligned with the advertised infrastructure-engineering scope without overstating seniority.
2. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, revise the first bullet to explicitly include technical ownership and stakeholder scope: “Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing; wrote the internal CI guide used in onboarding and supported teams in adopting the workflow.” Use only this wording if the guide and onboarding usage described elsewhere remain accurate.
3. In the same Odrava section, revise the ephemeral-environment bullets to make the supported systems-design and operational scope clearer: “Designed and built short-lived merge-request environments for applications, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster; environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.” Retain “shared Kubernetes cluster” and “namespace-level” limitations elsewhere so the CV does not imply cluster administration.
4. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, add the existing mentoring evidence as a final bullet: “Mentored two QA interns in 2023 and wrote an internal guide to CI pipelines used in onboarding.” This directly strengthens evidence for technical leadership, clear communication, and bringing colleagues along.
5. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section under “Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps,” change “Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS” to “Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS certificate management.” This uses the job ad’s security and certificate-management terminology while remaining truthful.
6. In the Technical Skills section, change the current “Monitoring & Security” heading to “Monitoring, TLS & Security Awareness” only if the listed evidence remains limited to Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, cert-manager, and TLS certificates. Do not add mTLS or broader security claims, because they are not supported by the candidate information.
7. In the Technical Skills section, make the Terraform scope more precise by changing “Terraform (personal projects)” to “Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS project)” and keep “Ansible (basic)” and “AWS (learning: EC2 and S3 basics)” explicitly qualified. This improves credibility for screening while avoiding an implication of professional cloud-infrastructure ownership.
8. In the “Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments” project, retain the specific stakeholder outcome but make it more prominent by changing the final bullet to: “Enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each ephemeral environment.” This directly supports collaboration and stakeholder alignment.
9. In the “CI Pipeline Speed-up” project, add the analytical framing already supported by the source material: “Profiled pipelines across three teams, identified parallelisation, dependency caching and test-stage separation opportunities, and reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes while lowering monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.” This better matches the requirement for strong analytical thinking.
10. In Education & Certifications, retain “Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam scheduled for January 2027,” but format it as “CKA exam scheduled — not yet passed (January 2027)” to eliminate any possible ATS or recruiter ambiguity about certification status.
